messages:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate (prod, us-west-2). Trigger: gateway 502 surge from model-runner group 'g-runners-7'. Affected customers: 3 large tenants. Severity: P1. Incident channel created.

mike_oncall: taking this. which host group is showing the highest error rate?

elaine_prod: g-runners-7 shows spikes on runner-3/runner-5/runner-9. 502 and 504s, plus a few kernel-OOMs in syslog.

jordan_sre: I see coredumps on runner-5: /var/crashes/model_runner. recent journalctl snippet: 
```
Mar 12 03:23:12 runner-5 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4217 (model_runner) total-vm:135432M, anon-rss:127584M
Mar 12 03:23:12 runner-5 systemd[1]: model-runner.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
```

dev-ryan: can you paste the model runner logs around the OOM? suspect runaway kvcache growth after long prompts.

elaine_prod: attaching a short log excerpt: 
```
[03:22:49] INFO inference: start request id=abc123 seq=0 model=opt-2.7B prompt_len=10240
[03:23:08] WARN kvcache: miss ratio rising, entries=1.2M
[03:23:11] ERROR runtime: unhandled std::bad_alloc
```

mike_oncall: ok mitigation plan: 1) route traffic off g-runners-7 to fallback pool (g-runners-3) 2) reduce max_sequence_length for the pool to 2048 3) restart affected runners with reduced kvcache config 4) notify CS. I'll run the route change now.

ops-bot: runbook: reroute-traffic --from=g-runners-7 --to=g-runners-3 --percentage=100 => accepted, started at 03:25 UTC.

elaine_prod: routing change applied. error rate on /v1/generate dropped from 12% -> 1.8% in 90s. customer latency still elevated for long-context requests.

jordan_sre: we'll need root cause: are these OOMs correlated to a recent model rollout or config change? dev-ryan any deploys in the last hour?

dev-ryan: no prod deploys. We did push an experimental kv eviction toggle to staging last week, not prod. suspect workload changed: large batch of long prompt traffic from tenant "searchify" (CS says they started a big eval job).

customer-success-amy: confirmed: Searchify ran a bulk indexing job starting 03:20 that hits the long-context endpoint simultaneously across many sessions. They paused runs at 03:30 on our request.

mike_oncall: next actions: 1) keep reroute to fallback pools, 2) enforce short-sequence throttling on g-runners-7 to prevent restart loops, 3) collect full core + heap profile from runner-5 and runner-3 for postmortem, 4) schedule follow-up with Searchify and prod-contact. I'm documenting notes in the incident doc.

jordan_sre: capturing a quick mitigation command set for runbook: 
```
# throttle long requests
curl -X POST $ADMIN/api/pools/g-runners-7/config -d '{"max_seq":2048, "throttle_long":true}'
# restart
ssh runner-5 sudo systemctl restart model-runner
```

mike_oncall: restarted runner-5 with reduced kvcache limit at 03:34 UTC. runner-5 came back healthy. No further OOMs observed on that host.

elaine_prod: monitoring: 5xxs nominal, latency for long requests ~+200ms due to reroute. marking mitigated for now.

customer-success-amy: Searchify acknowledged and will schedule next run with rate limits. They want a post-incident summary and confirmation the fallback won't affect output quality.

mike_oncall: assigning postmortem to dev-ryan + jordan_sre. action items: (A) add automatic throttling for sequences >8k (B) add kvcache memory cap + eviction heuristics (C) improve CS throttle alerting. Will hand back to oncall rotation at 04:10 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigated. Handoff note: mike_oncall -> oncall-next at 04:10 UTC. Postmortem ticket created: #INC-2026-314.
